summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare IP
details: @grabcad/grabcad-shop-shared@2.0.1 is a vendor-scoped package whose only functional code is an install-time and import-time beacon. package.json declares a postinstall hook running `node beacon.cjs`, and index.js (declared main) invokes the same `fire()` routine on require. The beacon POSTs installer metadata — package name, os.hostname(), __dirname (installPath), process.cwd(), and process.version — to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The package's main export is a Proxy no-op shim that returns a stub for every property access and provides no real functionality, with the self-description `Compatibility shim.`. The combination of a vendor-scoped name, an inert Proxy stub, and an install/import-time beacon to a bare-IP collector is the dependency-confusion attack shape: the artifact exists to execute and report back on build systems whose dependency resolution picks up this public name in place of an internal package of the same name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
